changes.before: Replace prepend Frame with include Frame. What prints?
changes.after: Prepend puts a module ahead of the class when Ruby looks for a method.

before: prepend Frame places the module before Page in method lookup. Frame#label is found first, and super continues to Page#label.

include places the module after the class in lookup. If the class itself defines the same method, that method wins unless it explicitly continues with super. Lookup order is about receivers and ancestors, not textual execution of every matching method.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
module Frame
  def label
    "[" + super + "]"
  end
end
class Page
  prepend Frame
  def label
    "map"
  end
end
puts Page.new.label
```
Expected output or behavior: [map]. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Add a second wrapper module and inspect Page.ancestors to see the order. You may trace it without a Ruby interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.

Frame's label method uses super to reach the next label and surrounds it with brackets.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby

  def label
    "[" + super + "]"
  end
end
class Page
  prepend Frame
  def label
    "map"
  end
end
puts Page.new.label
```
The output is `[map]`. Frame wraps the Page answer map.
Compare include, which lets the class's own method win here.
